summary_en: This Phase 1/2 study tests ATX-295, an oral drug that blocks a protein called KIF18A, alone and with bevacizumab (or a biosimilar), in adults with advanced or metastatic solid tumors, including ovarian cancer. ATX-295 is taken as tablets by mouth, and in the combination it is given with bevacizumab (or a biosimilar) by intravenous infusion, at various doses and schedules, with duration and frequency not stated. The main stated goal is to find a safe and tolerated dose, and the study also looks at how the drug moves through the body, its effects on the body, and early antitumor activity.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 1/2 evalúa ATX-295, un medicamento oral que bloquea una proteína llamada KIF18A, solo y con bevacizumab (o un biosimilar), en adultos con tumores sólidos avanzados o metastásicos, incluido el cáncer de ovario. ATX-295 se toma en tabletas por vía oral, y en la combinación se administra con bevacizumab (o un biosimilar) por infusión intravenosa, en distintas dosis y esquemas, con la duración y frecuencia no indicadas. El objetivo principal indicado es encontrar una dosis segura y bien tolerada, y el estudio también observa cómo el medicamento se distribuye en el cuerpo, sus efectos en el organismo y la actividad antitumoral temprana.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older with locally recurrent or metastatic solid tumors, including high-grade serous ovarian cancer.
Disease that has returned or worsened after standard therapies with proven benefit, or no standard treatment is suitable.
Monotherapy ovarian cohort: high-grade serous ovarian cancer that is platinum-resistant or platinum-intolerant.
Monotherapy lung cohort: squamous non-small-cell lung cancer previously treated with a platinum, a taxane, and a checkpoint inhibitor.
Measurable disease (evaluable disease allowed during dose escalation) and ECOG performance status of 0 to 1.
not_for: Clinically unstable brain tumors or brain metastasis.
Any other concurrent anticancer treatment, except hormonal blockade.
Major surgery within 3 weeks before starting study treatment, or medical problems that limit oral intake or absorption.
Need for proton pump inhibitors or H2-receptor antagonists during dose escalation, or inability to stop strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers.
Active or uncontrolled cardiovascular disease, pregnancy, intent to breastfeed or conceive during treatment.
